title: Joint Count Calibration of Personalization-Gain Intervals at Simultaneous Ranking Ties

gap_reasons: The delivered result is an exact interval construction and quantitative architecture separation on one stipulated shrinking Bernoulli experiment with a public center and radius; it does not resolve general personalization-gain inference at the tie boundary identified by [Li and Brunskill](https://arxiv.org/html/2607.08951v1). proof_attempt_summary: Discovery established exact finite-count 90%-honest connected intervals on the public-center shrinking Bernoulli boxes, attainable computable symmetric cutoff calibration with limiting scaled expected length at most 3.86, and an optimized-allocation shared-data separate-calibration summed-marginal-length converse above 4.2933. Math review and nine source checks pass, but D0.5 assigns incremental tier at ceiling 4.7 versus field 7.4, and an independent main audit confirms no bounded faithful repair. Unknown-center global honesty, sharp direct minimax length, maximizing geometry and practical complexity remain unproved; the accepted-bank comparator positioning finding is retained; no Lean formalization was attempted.
tldr: The causal personalization gain compares the best feature-specific treatment rule with the best constant treatment. In a stipulated randomized two-stratum, three-arm Bernoulli subexperiment, both rankings can tie simultaneously. Exact joint count calibration gives connected intervals with at least \(90\%\) coverage for every \(n>4225\), and uniform limiting scaled worst-case expected length at most \(2c^\dagger\leq3.86\). Its Gaussian cutoff is computably enclosed and attained by the exact-count cutoffs. Separately calibrated marginal interval subtraction has limiting scaled worst-case summed length at least \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{NP}}>4.2933\), even with optimized error allocation and shared data and randomness. This converse extends by restriction to every containing nonregular personalization experiment with the same observations and causal targets. The direct interval and upper bound remain specific to the Bernoulli subexperiment. Exact maximizing geometry and unrestricted or direct minimax expected length remain open.
gap: Li and Brunskill identify nonunique conditional and population optimizers as a boundary of their personalization-gain inference. Directional theory and likelihood-inclusion duality do not determine the optimal joint-error cutoff for this dual-tie target or transfer that cutoff to exact finite-count honesty.
fill: The joint-error cutoff is characterized by uniform Gaussian tail calibration, enclosed to arbitrary prescribed accuracy by a terminating continuum algorithm, and attained as the limit of exact semialgebraic count decisions. A certified overlap correction gives \(c^\dagger\leq1.93\), whereas signed calibration requires a cutoff above \(1.935\). The expected-length comparison and finite likelihood-ratio subtraction converse use identical laws, observations, target, coverage, and risk.
